Change one colour, change the rug

childNodes.textContent: He recognized this effect when searching for a method by which he could change the color combinations of his rug designs entirely by adding or changing 1 color only.

These two rugs use the same red, blue and yellow. Only the lines differ. With black lines the rug looks dark and rich. With white lines every colour looks lighter, as if it had been mixed with white. Make the pattern smaller and the effect gets stronger, because the eye starts mixing the lines into the colours.

childNodes.textContent: On paper Bezold had to redraw a design to test a change. Here the same pattern redraws in an instant, so you can flip one colour back and forth and watch the rest of the rug move with it.

attributes.class: mb-6 max-w-2xl font-serif text-lg italic leading-relaxed text-muted

childNodes.textContent: There is a special kind of optical mixture, the Bezold Effect, named after its discoverer, Wilhelm von Bezold (1837–1907).
Pick one part of the rug and change only that colour. Hold the button below to see the rug as it was before your change. Lines work best, because they touch every other colour.

childNodes.textContent: Thin lines that touch every colour change all of them at once
The smaller the pattern, the more the eye mixes the lines into the colours
White lines lighten a whole design and black lines deepen it, though no other colour changed
Bezold could restyle a rug by swapping one thread colour
In a UI, borders, dividers and icon strokes tint everything they touch, so check a palette change at real size, not on swatches
